title: General Training Task 1 - A letter
subtitle: Register, planning and checking
summary: Choose the right level of formality for the reader, plan the letter from the bullet points in the task, and check the tenses and prepositions that most often go wrong.

lesson.heading: Three registers, one decision
lesson.text: General Training Task 1 always asks for a letter, and the letter must be in the **correct style**. Who you are writing to decides everything else.

examples.text: **informal** - writing to family or friends
**semi-formal** - writing to a work colleague you know well
**formal** - writing to a business or a local newspaper

lesson.note: Read the situation in the task twice. *Write to the manager of the company* and *write to a friend who works there* need two completely different letters.

lesson.heading: The same four moves, three ways
rows: Thanks for the parcel, it just arrived!
I'm afraid I won't be able to attend the meeting next week.
I'm writing in response to your advertisement.
I can't wait to see you next week.
I'm looking forward to getting back to work.
I look forward to your reply
lesson.note: Contractions (*I'm*, *can't*) are fine in informal and semi-formal letters. In a formal letter, write the full forms.

lesson.heading: The task is also the plan
lesson.text: The bullet points in the question tell you exactly what to write about. Turn them into a seven-part plan and you have satisfied Task Achievement and Coherence and Cohesion at the same time.

examples.text: **1.** Greeting - *Dear Sir or Madam,*
**2.** Opening statements - introduce yourself and say why you are writing
**3.** Explain the situation
**4.** Describe the problem
**5.** Say what you would like to happen
**6.** Closing statements - signal the end of the letter
**7.** End the letter

lesson.note: Include **all** the points in the task and **only** relevant ideas. A vivid paragraph about something the task did not ask for lowers your Task Achievement score rather than raising it.

left.label: Content
examples: **Task Achievement:** Does your letter answer all the parts of the question? Are all your ideas relevant?
**Coherence and Cohesion:** Are your ideas well organised, clear and well connected?

right.label: Language
examples: **Lexical Resource:** Have you avoided repeating the same words and copying words from the question?
**Grammatical Range and Accuracy:** Have you made few mistakes and shown a range of structures?

lesson.heading: The tense mistakes that keep recurring
lesson.text: Decide when the event belongs before you choose the verb: something that **happened** in the past, **has happened** recently, **is true now**, **will happen** in the future, or that you **would like to** happen.

examples.text: *I hope that the above information ~~would~~ **will** be helpful to you.*
*I ~~will~~ **would** be grateful if you could think about the situation.*
*However, there ~~were~~ **are** a few things I have to comment on.*
*On the bus, I ~~spend~~ **spent** the entire journey trying to keep warm.*
*I want to describe the kind of area I ~~like~~ **would like** to move to.*
*I am ~~look~~ **looking** forward to **hearing** from you.*
*My uncle is going away, so he ~~need~~ **needs** someone to help run his business.*
*I ~~writing~~ **am writing** you this letter regarding a computer course.*

lesson.heading: Prepositions in a letter
lesson.text: Letters are full of fixed preposition patterns. These are worth memorising as whole phrases rather than as rules.

examples.text: an important examination **on** the following day
**on** the night **of** last Sunday
an advertisement **in** the newspaper
the main reason **for** my trip
looking forward **to** your reply and **to** having more details
contact me **on** my phone **at** home **on** 5467 4539
support the project **in** a lot of ways
experience **in / of** cooking and cleaning
really interested **in** this job

lesson.text: Task 2 is worth twice as many points as Task 1, so spend only 20 minutes here - and leave at least three of them to check spelling, punctuation and grammar. Take a reliable watch: mobile phones are not allowed in the exam room.

exercises.prompt: Sort these phrases by the register they belong to.

items.text: I'm looking forward to getting back to work.
I'm writing in response to your advertisement.

exercises.prompt: You are asked to write to a local newspaper. Which greeting and ending fit?
options: Dear Sir or Madam ... Yours sincerely
exercises.explanation: A newspaper is a business you do not know personally, so the letter is formal throughout - including the contractions you leave out.

exercises.prompt: Correct the tense: *I hope that the above information ___ be helpful to you.*
exercises.explanation: *Would* here suggests a condition that has not been stated. The writer simply means it will help.

exercises.prompt: Match each marking criterion with the question it asks.

pairs.right: Does the letter answer all parts of the question?
Are the ideas well organised and connected?
Have you avoided repeating and copying words?
Few mistakes, and a range of structures?

exercises.prompt: *I am really interested ___ this job and also have the ability to do it very well.*
exercises.explanation: *Interested in* is fixed. So are *the reason for*, *an advertisement in* and *looking forward to*.

exercises.statement: Adding an extra paragraph about something the task did not ask for shows range and raises your score.
exercises.explanation: Task Achievement asks whether all your ideas are relevant. Irrelevant content costs marks and uses time you need for checking.

exercises.prompt: *I am look forward to hear from you.* What is wrong?
options: It should be *I am looking forward to hearing from you*
It should be *I look forward to hear from you*
It should be *I am look forward to hearing from you*
exercises.explanation: *Am* needs the -ing form, and *forward to* is followed by a gerund - two of the commonest errors in one short phrase.

exercises.answer: I am writing in response to your advertisement in the newspaper.
exercises.explanation: *In response to* and *an advertisement in* are both fixed - and the full form *I am* keeps the register formal.

exercises.statement: General Training Writing Task 1 and Task 2 are worth the same number of points.
exercises.explanation: Task 2 is worth twice as much, so Task 1 gets 20 minutes and Task 2 gets 40.

exercises.prompt: *My uncle is going away on holiday, so he ___ someone to help run his business.* (need)
exercises.explanation: The -s on a third-person present verb is a small mark to lose, and one of the easiest to catch in a three-minute check.
